newsitem.title: USA: Commonwealth Edison VP defends Ill. dereg proposal.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth Edison VP defends Ill. dereg proposal.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Vice President Frank Clark defended a pending Illinois electric deregulation bill as providing "something for everyone" and said a regulatory panel's criticism was not unexpected.
Illinois Commerce Commission in a report Monday said the plan too heavily favors utilities and could discourage competition.
The panel questioned the size of rate reductions, lengthy transition periods and provisions for transitional funding of existing utilities.
"There was nothing in the report that was not expected," Clark said on Monday. "The report is consistent with other public discussions on this issue from the ICC."

Commonwealth Edison, a subsidiary of Unicom Corp, supported and helped draft the deregulation plans now pending. Illinois lawmakers are expected to continue the debate over the plan during their fall veto session.

The commission members focused on four main issues of concern out of a 256-page bill in a critique of parts they believe should be changed, Clark said. The numerous parts not addressed must pose no problem to the commission, he said.
"We think the bill has something for everyone, something that benefits everyone and also has a fairly rapid transition from the regulated to the deregulated or competitive market," Clark said.

The commission questioned whether allowing utilities to sell billions of securitized bonds to cover transition costs and allowing recovery of stranded cost investments over a 10-year period would stunt competition.
The report "doesn't purport to look at all sides," Clark said. "By raising the questions, they can now be addressed."
The bill would bring deregulation to businesses by 2000 and all residential customers by 2002, Clark added.
